design:
D1. The switch is a column on the agent beside can_accept_evidence, written only by the operator's agent-settings route. Rejected alternatives: a project-level grant table, or a charter flag. Both lose the "behaviour is not authority" rule at models.py:313-345.

D2. Superseded and held are marks on the document, not phases. The phase machine (TRANSITIONS) and its operator gates stay untouched, so approve and archive remain operator-only by the code that already enforces them. Rejected: a new 'superseded' phase, which would add transitions out of approved and exploring that every phase consumer would have to learn.

D3. An agent's fold calls spec_service.fold with archive=False, then marks the change superseded with the capability as its successor. Rejected: letting the agent's fold archive, because archive cannot be undone and the operator ruled it theirs.

D4. Each tidy act is a spec_document_events row of kind 'tidy'. A later operator row of kind 'tidy_reviewed' names the reviewed ids, the same shape as amendment and amendment_reviewed. Rejected: a new table, because the event log already carries actor and run and is append-only.

D5. Agents get one MCP tool, tidy_spec_document. It is listed only for an agent whose switch is on; the Hub refuses regardless of what the tool list shows.

D6. The live-work check reuses spec_lifecycle.open_task_ids and the running-build lookup the fold already uses.

CONTRACT (exact names the tasks and the drive share):
- Agent field `can_admin_specs: bool`, default false. It appears on the agent read and is accepted only on the operator's agent-settings update. Any agent-credential write of it is refused with 403.
- SpecDocument columns: superseded_at, superseded_by (actor name), superseded_reason, superseded_successor (path or null), held_at, held_note.
- Document read fields: `superseded: {at, by, reason, successor} | null` and `held: {at, note} | null`.
- Operator routes, on the existing spec router in hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py beside POST /documents/phase:
  - POST /documents/{path}/hold with body {note} returns the document. DELETE /documents/{path}/hold releases it.
  - The documents list accepts `superseded=true`.
  - POST /documents/archive-batch with body {paths: [..]} returns {archived: [paths], refused: [{path, code, reason}]}.
  - GET /tidy-acts?reviewed=false returns [{id, act, path, agent, run_id, at, reason, code_wins}]. code_wins is {requirement, before, after, cited} or null.
  - POST /tidy-acts/reviewed with body {ids: [..]} or {all: true}.
- MCP tool `tidy_spec_document(path, op, reason, ...)`. op is one of fold, create_capability, edit_capability, supersede, clear_superseded, set_slice.
  - fold takes capability plus the fold options of spec_service.fold (items, retire, retire_criteria, algorithms, criteria).
  - create_capability takes title, optional area and optional fold_from.
  - edit_capability takes requirement, statement or retire=true, and optional code_wins {cited}.
  - supersede takes optional successor.
  - set_slice takes roadmap and slice.
  - It returns {ok, act_id} or a refusal {code, reason}.
- Refusal codes: spec_admin_off, document_held, live_work, reason_required, operators_act.
- Event kinds: tidy and tidy_reviewed.

GUARDS RELAXED:
- ck_spec_document_merges_actor_is_operator becomes: actor_kind = 'operator' OR (actor_kind = 'agent' AND run_id IS NOT NULL). It adds run_id to spec_document_merges if absent.
- spec_service.py:171 capability_write_is_the_operators admits an agent with can_admin_specs.
- Any Hub test asserting that every agent is refused a capability write is narrowed to agents with the switch off.

lifecycle: Ships as slice 1 of 'The specs stay true and easy to work with'. After the operator restarts :8000 on the migrated build, they turn the switch on for one agent and ask it to tidy this repository's 48 built, unfolded changes as its first real job.

problem: Every act that keeps a corpus true is the operator's today: folding a change into a capability, writing or retiring a capability, archiving. That is enforced in code and in the database (spec_lifecycle.py:358/364, spec_service.py:134/171, and the CHECK constraint ck_spec_document_merges_actor_is_operator at models.py:2627, migration 0074). No agent tool exists for any of them. The work therefore does not get done. On this repository only 4 folds have ever happened, none since 2026-10-29, while 48 approved changes are fully built and unfolded. So the capability specs describe the system as of early October, and a stale specification is worse than none, because readers trust it. The operator wants to ask an agent to "fix my specs" and have it able to do the whole job, without giving up approval or archiving, which cannot be undone.

requirements.rationale: Authority sits on the agent record and nowhere else, as with can_accept_evidence (models.py:313-345): a charter is behaviour text a model reads, and prose an agent can be persuaded to write must never become an authorisation mechanism.
requirements.statement: Each agent has a spec-admin switch, off for every existing and new agent, that only the operator can change. The agent's settings page shows it and lets the operator change it.

An agent with the switch on can, through its tools: fold an approved change into an existing capability with the same choices the operator's fold offers (which requirements, retired requirements and criteria, rewritten criteria, algorithms); create a capability and fold into it; edit a capability's content, including rewriting or retiring a requirement; mark any change, roadmap, area or capability superseded, or clear that mark; and set or correct a change's roadmap slice. Each act has the same effect on the document's content as the operator's own act.

requirements.rationale: The operator's choice (2026-11-08): archive cannot be undone (spec_lifecycle TRANSITIONS has no way out of archived), so agents mark and the operator archives. A mark that can be cleared makes an agent's mistake cheap.
requirements.statement: A document marked superseded keeps its phase, content and history, shows that it is superseded, by whom, why and, where given, by which document, and cannot be built. Clearing the mark restores it as it was. A fold by an agent marks the folded change superseded by the capability instead of archiving it.

The operator can filter the project's documents to those marked superseded, see for each who marked it, why and its successor, and archive any selection of them, or all, in one action. Archiving stays the operator's alone.

requirements.rationale: The operator's rule (2026-11-08): documents they held stay held. Today a hold exists only as prose in spec-queue/METRICS.md (decision trace-6), which no gate can read.
requirements.statement: The operator can hold any document, with an optional note, and release it. A tidy act on a held document is refused, naming the hold. The agent may ask the operator whether to supersede a held document; the hold stays until the operator releases it.

requirements.rationale: Approval authorises building and archive cannot be undone; the operator has decided only they do either (2026-11-08).
requirements.statement: The switch never lets an agent approve a document, close an exploration, archive, accept or decline a proposed amendment, answer a cannot-satisfy report, decide evidence, or hold or release a document. These stay refused for an agent whatever its switch says.
An agent with the switch off that attempts any tidy act is refused with a reason that names the switch and says only the operator can turn it on, and nothing changes.

requirements.rationale: The operator's rule (2026-11-08): specs with a build in progress are not touched. Builders and reviewers work against the document as approved.
requirements.statement: A tidy act is refused on any document that has a running build or open tasks, and on a capability while a document with a running build is being folded into it, naming what is in progress.

requirements.rationale: The operator chose apply-at-once over propose-and-accept (2026-11-08): 48 folds needing 48 approvals defeats the purpose. Visibility replaces the gate, as for tester amendments.
requirements.statement: Every tidy act applies at once and is recorded with the agent, its run, the time, the act, the document and the agent's reason. The operator sees every act not yet reviewed in one list, can open the document each touched, and can mark acts reviewed one at a time or all at once. The record is kept after review and the agent cannot change or remove it.
A tidy act without a non-empty reason is refused, naming the missing reason.

requirements.rationale: The operator allowed the agent to decide code-versus-spec disagreements (2026-11-08). A requirement changed to match an accident makes the accident permanent, so the change must be visible and cite what it rests on.
requirements.statement: When an agent rewrites or retires a requirement because the code does something else, the act records that the requirement was changed to match the code, the requirement before and after, and the code or test the agent read to decide. The operator's list marks such acts apart from the others.
The switch, the marks and the tidy acts behave the same in every project, with no dependence on this repository's layout or document names.

in: A per-agent spec-admin switch, off by default, that only the operator can turn on or off

Agent tidy acts: fold an approved change into an existing or new capability; edit a capability, including rewriting or retiring a requirement the code contradicts; mark a document superseded or clear that mark; set or correct a change's roadmap slice
A superseded mark on documents, reversible, with who, why and by what, and an operator filter of superseded documents with a batch archive
An operator hold on documents that refuses tidy acts on them
A record of every tidy act with agent, run and reason, listed for the operator until marked reviewed
Works the same in any project
non_goals: Approving any document, closing exploration, accepting or declining proposed amendments, answering cannot-satisfy reports, deciding evidence, and archiving. These stay the operator's whether or not the switch is on
Touching a document whose build is running or which has open tasks
Reorganising the corpus on disk or in the index (the later slices of 'The specs stay true and easy to work with')
Granting the switch through a charter, a message, or an agent's own request
Making archive reversible; archive stays permanent and the operator's

summary: The operator can switch on, for one agent, the right to keep a project's specification corpus true. That agent can fold built changes into capabilities, create and edit capabilities (rewriting or retiring a requirement the code contradicts), mark documents superseded, and fix roadmap links. Its acts apply at once and are listed for the operator to review. The operator alone approves and archives: they filter the superseded documents and archive them in a batch. Documents the operator holds, and documents with a build in progress, are refused to the agent; for a held one, the agent may ask the operator whether to supersede it.
